Answers to the questions and error messages that come up most often while
working through the [bp-submission-pipeline manual](index.qmd). Each entry
links back to the step it's drawn from, so you can jump to the full context.

Can't find what you're looking for, or need to reach a person? See
[Support](support.qmd).

## B. GitHub access

<details>
<summary>The browser doesn't open when I run `gh auth login`</summary>

`gh` also prints a one-time code and a URL in the terminal. Open
`https://github.com/login/device` manually, enter the code, and complete the
sign-in there. See [B. GitHub access](bp-submission-pipeline/github-access.qmd).
</details>

## C. Install package

<details>
<summary>`make pull` fails with "lacks the read:packages scope"</summary>

Your GitHub token doesn't have the scope Docker needs to pull private images
yet. Run `gh auth refresh -s read:packages`, then try again. See
[B. GitHub access](bp-submission-pipeline/github-access.qmd) and [C. Install package](bp-submission-pipeline/install-package.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Cloning fails with "repository not found" or "access denied"</summary>

Your GitHub account hasn't been granted access to the private repository yet.
Request access via [Support](support.qmd) before retrying. See
[C. Install package](bp-submission-pipeline/install-package.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make pull` fails with "no such file or directory" on `/var/run/docker.sock`</summary>

The Docker daemon isn't running. Start Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or run
`systemctl start docker` (Linux), then run `make pull` again. See
[C. Install package](bp-submission-pipeline/install-package.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>The submodule folders are empty after cloning</summary>

The repository was cloned without `--recurse-submodules`. Delete the cloned
folder and re-run the full clone command. See
[C. Install package](bp-submission-pipeline/install-package.qmd).
</details>

## D. Configure

<details>
<summary>`make dirs` fails with "Permission denied"</summary>

`PIPELINE_ROOT` points at a mount owned by root. Transfer ownership with
`sudo chown -R 1000:1000 <mount>`, then re-run `make dirs` as a regular user —
never with `sudo`. See [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` reports the salt is unchanged</summary>

The `salt` value in `config.yaml` still matches the shipped example. Open the
file, replace it with your own secret (≥ 32 characters), and re-run
`make doctor`. See [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>I get an auth error after changing the salt</summary>

The salt was changed *after* `make gen-credentials` already hashed a
password with the old one, invalidating it. Rotate the salt once, then
re-run `make gen-credentials` with the current salt. See
[D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd) and [F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make` commands fail on Windows</summary>

They must be run in **Git Bash**, not PowerShell or cmd.exe. Also confirm
`.env` was saved with LF (Unix) line endings, not CRLF. See
[D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd).
</details>

## E1. model.json

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` (or setup) reports "model.json missing"</summary>

Run `make setup-refdata` again and confirm `model.json` appears in
`PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR`. See [E1. model.json](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-model.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>I see "Warning: model.json not found in bigpicture-slidetap/tests/test_data"</summary>

The pipeline's Git submodules weren't initialised. Run
`git submodule update --init --recursive`, then retry `make setup-refdata`.
See [E1. model.json](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-model.qmd).
</details>

## E2. mappers.xlsx

<details>
<summary>An operator's input ends up as an empty attribute after export</summary>

No mapping key matched it. Check the relevant sheet in `mappers.xlsx` for
regex anchoring, typos, or a case mismatch. The operator's original input
isn't lost — fix the mapping row, re-upload `mappers.xlsx`, and re-trigger
mapping from the curation UI; no workbook re-submission is needed. See
[E2. mappers.xlsx](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-mappers.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>A mapper seems to be silently missing from the running pipeline</summary>

Check the pipeline logs for a `logging.warning` or `logging.exception` line
at startup. Common causes: a wrong `Sheet` name in the master sheet, an
invalid UUID in the `UID` column, or an unknown `Type` value. See
[E2. mappers.xlsx](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-mappers.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make setup-refdata` warns "mappers.xlsx not found in ..."</summary>

Same cause as the `model.json` version of this warning: the pipeline's Git
submodules weren't initialised. Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`,
then retry `make setup-refdata`. See
[E2. mappers.xlsx](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-mappers.qmd).
</details>

## F. TLS + credentials

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says the certificate or key is missing</summary>

Re-run `make ssl`, then check that `PIPELINE_SSL_DIR`, `PIPELINE_SSL_CERT`,
and `PIPELINE_SSL_KEY` in `.env` match the files it created. See
[F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` rejects `PIPELINE_SSL_CERT`/`PIPELINE_SSL_KEY` as "not a path", or `make ssl` fails with a doubled path like `./data/certs/./data/certs/`</summary>

One of the two variables holds a path instead of a bare filename. Set it back
to a filename, e.g. `server.crt` — see
[F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd#if-something-goes-wrong) for why.
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says the credentials file is missing</summary>

Re-run `make gen-credentials`. It writes to the repo root by default — make
sure `PIPELINE_CREDENTIALS_FILE` in `.env` points at that file. See
[F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>I can't log in even though the certificate and credentials files exist</summary>

The password was almost certainly hashed with a different salt than the app
is currently using. Set the salt in `config.yaml` first, then re-run
`make gen-credentials` so the hash matches. See
[F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd) and [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd).
</details>

## G. Preflight + boot

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says a cert, key, or credentials file is missing</summary>

You skipped or mis-set [F. TLS + credentials](bp-submission-pipeline/tls-credentials.qmd). Re-run
`make ssl` and `make gen-credentials`. See
[G. Preflight + boot](bp-submission-pipeline/boot.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says the config still matches the example / the salt is not rotated</summary>

Rotate the salt in [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd), then re-run
`make gen-credentials` so your login still matches. See
[G. Preflight + boot](bp-submission-pipeline/boot.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says a host path is missing or not owned by UID 1000</summary>

Create the local data tree with `make dirs` (single-host setups), or fix the
mount ownership — see [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd). See also
[G. Preflight + boot](bp-submission-pipeline/boot.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make doctor` says `gh` is not logged in</summary>

Re-run the sign-in from [B. GitHub access](bp-submission-pipeline/github-access.qmd). See
[G. Preflight + boot](bp-submission-pipeline/boot.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>The browser can't reach the UI after `make up`</summary>

Give it a few seconds and refresh — first boot can take up to a minute. If it
still fails, check `make logs` for a service that failed to start, and
confirm nothing else is using the port in `PIPELINE_PORT`. See
[G. Preflight + boot](bp-submission-pipeline/boot.qmd).
</details>

## H. Run a submission test

<details>
<summary>Parse produces no items after I upload the workbook</summary>

The workbook's format doesn't match what the pipeline expects. Check you're
uploading the correct `.xlsx` and that its sheet layout matches the import
schema. See [H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Images stay "failed" even after I click Retry</summary>

Check `make logs` for the image worker's output. Common causes: the slide
file isn't reachable at the path referenced in the workbook, or DICOM
conversion failed on that specific file format. See
[H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>The Post-process Start button is greyed out</summary>

One or more items are still invalid. Return to **Curate**, fix the mapping
for the flagged items in `mappers.xlsx`, and remap. See
[H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd) and
[E2. mappers.xlsx](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-mappers.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>The Submit button is greyed out on the Export page</summary>

The project hasn't reached **Completed** status yet. Confirm the batch was
completed and check the batch status chip in the Batch sidebar. See
[H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Export never reaches "Export Complete" and reverts to "Completed" with no error</summary>

An observation is missing a required coded attribute (e.g. `diagnose`) that
has no `"optional": true` flag in `model.json`. Check `make logs` for a
`ValueError` naming the missing attribute's tag — export stops at the first
one it hits, so fixing one observation can just surface the next.

**A green status in Curate does not rule this out, and it is not simply
"stale."** For an attribute nested inside another attribute — a diagnosis or
other pathology code inside an observation is the normal case — **Remap**
recomputes the correct value and marks the item valid, but never writes that
value back to the database: the validity flag and the mapping's hit count
both update, the value itself does not. The item is wrong from the moment
you click Remap, and Remap will keep reporting success no matter how many
times you run it.

**Do not remap a nested attribute. Clear the affected mappers and re-parse
instead** — delete the batch (or start a fresh project) and re-upload the
workbook. Re-parsing maps the value *before* the item is created, which is
the code path that persists it correctly; remap only runs *after* the item
already exists, which is the path that drops it.

For a plain (non-nested) attribute, re-checking the mapping in
`mappers.xlsx` and remapping does work — this failure is specific to
attributes nested inside another attribute.

Alternatively, fix by supplying the missing value from the source workbook
data, or by marking the attribute optional in `model.json` and restarting
the stack — only for attributes your site added, never for BigPicture's
MSMDAD attributes, and note this loses the value rather than recovering it.
See [H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd) and
[E1. model.json](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-model.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make export-check` reports "FAIL outbox not found"</summary>

The `PIPELINE_STORAGE` path in `.env` doesn't exist or isn't mounted
correctly. See [D. Configure](bp-submission-pipeline/configure.qmd) and
[H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make export-check` reports "FAIL no project directories"</summary>

The export didn't finish writing. Check `make logs` and confirm the project
status shows **Export Complete** in the UI — if it shows **Completed**
instead, see the entry above on a missing required attribute, which also
prevents the bundle from being written. See
[H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

## I. Validate the bundle

<details>
<summary>`validate-upload` fails with "dataset directory not found"</summary>

The path passed to `DATASET=` doesn't exist. Double-check the path and make
sure the export step finished successfully. See
[I. Validate the bundle](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`validate-upload` fails with "missing required folder"</summary>

The export didn't create the expected bundle structure. Re-export from the
UI; if the folder is still missing, check `make logs` for export worker
errors. See [I. Validate the bundle](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`validate-upload` fails with a schema validation error</summary>

A metadata XML file doesn't conform to the BigPicture XSD schema — usually a
mismatch between your `model.json` or `mappers.xlsx` and the current
metaflex schema. Check the named file and element, or pinpoint it by hand
with `xmllint` — see [Validate metadata](direct-upload/validate-metadata.qmd).
See also [I. Validate the bundle](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`staining.xml` has a separate, near-identical `STAINING` entry for every slide, even when they're all the same stain</summary>

This is expected, not a mapping bug. In the BigPicture metadata standard, a
Slide's `STAINING_INFORMATION_REF` points to exactly one Staining Entity —
there's no mechanism for multiple slides to share one. So a dataset where
every slide is plain H&E still gets one `STAINING` block per slide, each with
its own generated alias, all carrying identical content (same
`staining_method`, same SNOMED code). Check `sample.xml` — each `SLIDE`
element's `STAINING_INFORMATION_REF` resolves to a different
`STAINING_PROCEDURE_*` alias in `staining.xml`, one per slide. See
[Staining mapping](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-staining.qmd) and
[I. Validate the bundle](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd).
</details>

## J. Upload to BigPicture

<details>
<summary>`make upload` fails with "TARGET is required"</summary>

`make upload` never guesses the destination. Re-run with `TARGET=staging`
(the A–J manual) or `TARGET=production`. See
[J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make upload` fails with "Invalid TARGET '<x>'"</summary>

The `TARGET` value is mistyped. Use exactly `staging` or `production`. See
[J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>I get "Missing creds file" for `s3cmd-inbox.conf` or `crypt4gh_bp_key.pub`</summary>

One of the two NBIS-provided files is absent from the credentials directory
for the `TARGET` you chose — `certs/staging` for `TARGET=staging`,
`certs/production` for `TARGET=production`. Place the missing file there and
retry. See [J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make upload` fails with "DATASET not set"</summary>

Re-run the command with `DATASET=<project_dir>/DATASET_<alias>` — the bundle's
path relative to the outbox root, not just the project directory name from
your `make export-check` output. See [J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make upload` fails with "Dataset dir not found"</summary>

The `<project_dir>/DATASET_<alias>` value doesn't match what's under
`PIPELINE_OUTBOX_DIR`. Confirm `<project_dir>` from the `make export-check`
output in [H. Run a submission test](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd), then check the
`DATASET_<alias>` subfolder actually exists inside it. See also
[J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>I get a connection or authentication error during upload</summary>

Your `s3cmd-inbox.conf` may be expired or misconfigured. Contact
[Support](support.qmd) for an updated file. See
[J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>My upload stalls partway and doesn't resume</summary>

Delete `upload.db` from your `PIPELINE_SUBMITTER_STATE` directory and retry
from the beginning. See [J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary>`make upload-persistent` fails with "tmux not found"</summary>

Install `tmux` on the machine running the command, or use plain
`make upload` instead — `tmux` is only needed for uploads run over an SSH
connection that might drop. See [J. Upload to BigPicture](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

## After submission

<details>
<summary>I submitted without a landing page</summary>

`landing_page.xml` is optional at submission time, so a missing one doesn't
block upload — you don't need to resubmit the dataset to add it. See
[Add a landing page after submission](add-landing-page.qmd) for the current
process.
</details>
